title: Cache-Line Aligned MemTable Layout and Deterministic SSTable Flush Compaction in a Rust LSM-Tree Implementation
topic: Log-Structured Merge-Tree (LSM-Tree) MemTable and SSTable Flush Compaction
domain: Storage Engines, Log-Structured Storage, Systems Architecture
description: Log-Structured Merge-Trees (LSM-trees) achieve high write throughput by buffering updates in an in-memory MemTable and periodically flushing sorted runs to disk-resident SSTables. This paper presents an empirical evaluation of a cache-line aligned Rust LSM-tree MemTable and flush compaction architecture, evaluated live on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900HX.
abstract: Log-Structured Merge-Trees (LSM-trees) achieve high write throughput by buffering updates in an in-memory MemTable and periodically flushing sorted runs to disk-resident SSTables. In modern cloud workloads, contention on cache lines and the cost of atomic synchronization dominate latency during MemTable insertion and SSTable compaction. This paper presents a Rust implementation that (i) aligns the MemTable's B-Tree nodes to cache-line boundaries, (ii) employs lock-free ring buffers for write ordering, and (iii) guarantees deterministic flush ordering through a monotonic sequence number barrier. We formalize two invariants---total-order of keys across flushed runs and height-balance of the in-memory B-Tree---and prove that they are preserved under concurrent execution. Empirical evaluation across 30 wall-clock iterations on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900HX (24 cores, 32 threads, 63.8 GB RAM, Windows 11) yields an observed mean latency of 15,115.62 µs (P50: 11,857.30 µs) and sustained throughput of 66,157 ops/s, validating logarithmic search envelopes O(log N) and bounded write latency. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/rust-algorithms/tree/main/algorithms/20261005_053754_lsm-tree_memtable_and_sstable}
